intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Hanauma Bay offers calm, clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles, making it perfect for beginner and experienced snorkelers alike. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian culture with a full evening of traditional dance performances, fire knife shows, and an all-you-can-eat Hawaiian feast including kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert. Interactive village exhibits let kids learn about six Pacific Island cultures throughout the day before the evening show.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Group lessons are family-friendly and suitable for children aged 5 and up. Most first-timers stand up on their board within the first session, creating unforgettable memories for the whole family.

experiences.name: Road to Hana Scenic Drive & Waterfalls
experiences.description: Embark on one of the world's most scenic coastal drives along Maui's northeastern coastline, stopping at lush rainforest waterfalls, black sand beaches, and bamboo forests. Family highlights include the Twin Falls swimming hole, Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach, and roadside fruit stands selling fresh coconuts and banana bread. Pack a picnic and make a full day of it.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Discover Hawaii's beloved food culture in the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore. Start with the famous rainbow shave ice at Matsumoto's, then explore local food trucks and restaurants serving fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp plates, and acai bowls. The town's laid-back vibe and colorful shops make it a perfect half-day family outing that won't break the budget.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late arrival night
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late arrival night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive via Flight UA at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Take a short stroll to the beach to enjoy the night ocean breeze and decompress from travel. Pick up snacks and essentials at a nearby convenience store or ABC Store.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport before baggage claim or pick up snacks at ABC Store near the resort (~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive late, so focus on settling in. Confirm resort check-in details in advance since it is after 10 PM. Pack light snacks in your carry-on for the late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy the beachfront view from the resort. Head down to the resort beach for a morning swim and explore the shoreline. Collect shells, watch surfers, and soak up the Hawaiian sunrise. Free activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a cheap local bus to a nearby snorkeling spot. Rent basic snorkel gear from a local beach shack (~$10-15/person) and explore the coral reef and tropical fish. Look for free public beach access points to avoid paid entry fees.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. Explore the nearby beachfront area on foot and enjoy the laid-back Hawaiian evening atmosphere. Look for free hula or live music performances at local shopping centers or beach parks.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee from a local farmers market or convenience store (~$8-10 per person)
meals.lunch: Visit a local food truck near the beach for plate lunch (rice, mac salad, protein) (~$10-13 per person)
meals.dinner: L&L Hawaiian Barbecue or similar local chain for an affordable Hawaiian plate dinner (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your first full day, so keep it relaxed and close to the resort. Pick up a weekly bus pass if available to save on transport costs throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby state or county beach park early in the morning for a family-friendly swim session. Many Hawaiian beach parks have free parking, restrooms, and picnic areas. Arrive early to secure a shaded spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local botanical garden or nature park. Many Hawaiian botanical gardens offer free or low-cost admission (~$5-10 per person). Walk through native Hawaiian plant collections and enjoy the lush tropical scenery with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local night market or farmers market if one is running. Browse local crafts, sample Hawaiian snacks like malasadas, shave ice, and fresh pineapple. Great for kids and budget-friendly browsing.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast with groceries from a local supermarket like Foodland or Times Supermarket — cereal, milk, bananas (~$5-7 per person)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the beach park with sandwiches, chips, and juice bought from a supermarket (~$6-8 per person)
meals.dinner: Try a local ramen or pho spot for an affordable and filling family dinner (~$10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stop by a local supermarket today to stock up on breakfast items, snacks, and drinks to keep daily food costs down. Having a small cooler is very helpful for beach picnics.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free or low-cost hike on a nearby trail with ocean or valley views. Many Hawaiian trails are free to access and offer stunning panoramic views. Start early to avoid midday heat and bring plenty of water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free or low-admission cultural site such as a historic Hawaiian heiau (temple), a local museum, or a cultural center. Learn about native Hawaiian history and traditions together as a family.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort beach for a family beach bonfire if permitted, or enjoy a quiet beachside evening. Look for free stargazing opportunities — Hawaii has some of the clearest night skies in the world.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl from a local cafe or food truck (~$10-12 per person) — a Hawaiian staple worth trying
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and sandwiches from the supermarket for the hike (~$5-7 per person)
meals.dinner: Local Hawaiian plate lunch spot or poke bowl restaurant for an early dinner (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for hiking and apply reef-safe sunscreen. Bring a reusable water bottle and refill it — staying hydrated in the Hawaiian heat is essential, especially for kids.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a calm, family-friendly beach known for safe swimming conditions. Look for beaches with lifeguards on duty for added safety with children. Build sandcastles, play in the waves, and enjoy the morning before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local aquarium or marine education center if available in the area. These are usually budget-friendly (~$10-15 per person) and educational for kids. Learn about Hawaiian marine life including sea turtles, reef fish, and coral ecosystems.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a free or low-cost luau preview or cultural performance. Many resorts and shopping centers host free mini cultural shows. Alternatively, look for a free community event or movie night on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and eggs at a local diner or breakfast spot (~$10-12 per person)
meals.lunch: Shave ice and a hot dog or corn dog from a beach concession stand (~$8-10 per person) — fun and affordable for kids
meals.dinner: Visit a local pizza or pasta place for a family-friendly budget dinner (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check local event listings online or at the resort concierge desk for any free community events happening this evening. Many Hawaiian communities host free outdoor events during summer months.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic coastal drive or bus ride to explore a different part of the island. Stop at scenic lookout points for photos and enjoy the dramatic coastal cliffs and ocean views. Most lookout points are free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a secluded or less-crowded beach for an afternoon of swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing. Pack a picnic lunch and spend a few hours exploring tide pools and watching for sea turtles resting on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a leisurely evening walk along the beachfront promenade. Browse local shops for affordable souvenirs like postcards, keychains, and small Hawaiian crafts.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie and granola from a local health food cafe or juice bar (~$8-10 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic with deli sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from the supermarket (~$6-8 per person)
meals.dinner: Try a local Mexican or Asian fusion restaurant for an affordable and flavorful dinner (~$11-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a car for the day, compare rates online and book in advance for the best budget deals. Alternatively, use the local bus system which is very affordable and covers most tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local farmers market in the morning. Hawaiian farmers markets are vibrant, colorful, and full of fresh tropical fruits, local honey, macadamia nuts, and handmade goods. Great for sampling local flavors at low cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a state beach park with facilities for family activities. Play beach volleyball, swim, or simply relax under a palm tree. Many parks have free BBQ grills available on a first-come basis.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a DIY beach BBQ at the park using a rented or park-provided grill. Pick up affordable meats, corn, and vegetables from the supermarket and enjoy a family cookout on the beach as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruits, pastries, and local coffee from the farmers market (~$8-12 per person)
meals.lunch: Snacks and light bites from the farmers market — try fresh coconut, pineapple, and local chips (~$6-8 per person)
meals.dinner: DIY beach BBQ with supermarket groceries — burgers, hot dogs, corn on the cob (~$10-13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive early at the beach park to claim a BBQ grill spot as they fill up quickly, especially on weekends. Bring charcoal, lighter fluid, and utensils from the supermarket.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning kayak or stand-up paddleboard session at a calm bay or lagoon. Many rental shops offer affordable hourly rates (~$15-20/hour). Paddling in the calm morning waters is a magical and budget-friendly Hawaiian experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free historic site, lighthouse, or state monument in the area. Walk around and learn about the history of the island. Many of these sites have free admission and offer beautiful photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort. Use the resort pool and beach amenities. Play card games or board games as a family. Look for any free resort entertainment such as live music or cultural demonstrations.

meals.breakfast: Grab and go breakfast burritos or sandwiches from a local cafe (~$8-10 per person)
meals.lunch: Plate lunch from a local Hawaiian diner near the historic site (~$10-13 per person)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using the resort kitchenette if available, or pick up ready-made meals from a supermarket deli (~$8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check if your resort accommodation has a kitchenette or microwave to prepare simple meals and save on dining costs. Supermarket deli sections in Hawaii often have excellent ready-made local dishes at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full morning at your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the Hawaiian sun. Take lots of photos and enjoy the peaceful morning before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local souvenir shop or craft market to pick up affordable gifts and mementos. Look for locally made items like Hawaiian quilts, koa wood products, and Aloha shirts at discount or outlet stores for the best value.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to a slightly upgraded dinner experience to celebrate the end of the trip. Look for early bird specials or happy hour deals at a mid-range Hawaiian restaurant to enjoy a festive meal without breaking the budget.

meals.breakfast: Malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from a local bakery — a Hawaiian tradition (~$5-7 per person)
meals.lunch: Poke bowl from a local poke shop — fresh, healthy, and affordable (~$12-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a local Hawaiian restaurant with fresh seafood or traditional Hawaiian dishes — look for early bird specials (~$18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start packing tonight to make the departure day less stressful. Check resort checkout time and arrange for luggage storage if needed for the final morning. Keep receipts for any travel expense reimbursements.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take a final swim in the ocean and say goodbye to the Hawaiian waves. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast before checkout. Pack all belongings and do a final room check.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort and store luggage if your flight is later in the day. Spend remaining time exploring the local area on foot — visit a nearby beach park, grab a final shave ice, or browse a local market one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Enjoy a final Hawaiian meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant. Reflect on the memories made and the beauty of the Hawaiian Islands.

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast — loco moco (rice, hamburger patty, egg, gravy) at a local diner (~$10-13 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a nearby cafe or food truck before heading to the airport (~$8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final quick meal near the airport (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport check-in, security, and boarding. Return any rental equipment and settle any resort charges before checkout. Keep a small amount of cash for tips and last-minute purchases.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront room and unwind with a light snack from the resort's late-night amenities.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at a layover airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport upon arrival — try the ABC Store or a casual airport eatery for local snacks like spam musubi or a plate lunch

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Pack light carry-on snacks for the journey. Confirm resort late-night check-in arrangements in advance. Exchange currency or withdraw cash at the airport ATM if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow start after the late arrival. After a leisurely breakfast, take a gentle stroll along the beachfront directly from the resort. Let the kids splash in the calm shore waters and get acquainted with the Hawaiian ocean environment. No pressure — just rest and acclimatize.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (a short drive or walk from most Oahu beachfront resorts) for your first real Hawaiian beach experience. Rent boogie boards or snorkel sets from a beachside vendor. Explore the shallow reef areas and enjoy the iconic Waikiki shoreline with the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki. Browse local shops and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Watch the sunset from the beach before heading to dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or in-room dining — a relaxed start to the day
meals.lunch: Lulu's Surf Club on Waikiki Beach — casual, oceanfront, family-friendly with burgers, fish tacos, and salads in the mid-range price point
meals.dinner: Eggs 'n Things (open late) or Duke's Waikiki — a beloved Waikiki institution with fresh seafood, hula pie dessert, and a fun family atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen before any beach activity — it's required at many Hawaii beaches and protects the coral. Stay hydrated throughout the day. This is a recovery and orientation day, so keep the pace gentle.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hanauma Bay for Snorkeling. Arrive by 7:00–7:30 AM to secure parking and avoid the midday crowds. All first-time visitors must watch a short marine education video before entering. The bay's calm, crystal-clear waters are perfect for families — kids and adults alike will marvel at the sea turtles, colorful reef fish, and vibrant coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Rinse off, relax at the resort pool or beachfront, and let the kids recharge. Alternatively, explore nearby Diamond Head State Monument for a short, rewarding family hike with panoramic views of Oahu (approximately 1.5 miles round trip, suitable for older kids).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening near the resort. Walk along the beach at sunset and take in the golden hour views from your beachfront location.

meals.breakfast: Pack a light breakfast or grab granola bars and fruit before heading to Hanauma Bay — no food is sold inside the reserve
meals.lunch: Kaimana Beach Café near Sans Souci Beach — casual, affordable, and close to Hanauma Bay's return route, offering fresh poke bowls and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods in Honolulu — an authentic, beloved local spot serving traditional Hawaiian plates like kalua pig, lomi salmon, and poi at very reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay has a daily visitor cap — book your entry reservation online in advance at the official Hawaii DLNR site. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes, and an underwater camera or waterproof phone case. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach. Book a 2-hour group lesson with a certified surf school (Hans Hedemann Surf School or Waikiki Surf Club are excellent family-friendly options). The gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki are ideal for first-timers of all ages. Instructors are experienced with children and beginners — most people stand up on their first lesson!
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, walk over to the Honolulu Zoo or the Waikiki Aquarium — both are just minutes from Waikiki Beach and perfect for younger children. The Aquarium features Hawaiian marine life up close and connects well to the morning's ocean theme.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This is a full evening event (typically starts at 12:00 PM for cultural village exploration, with the luau dinner and Ha: Breath of Life show in the evening). Book the evening package if doing a half-day visit, or plan this as a full-day event on a different day. For today, enjoy a cultural show or live music at a beachside venue.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — fuel up before surf lessons
meals.lunch: Barefoot Bar at Duke's Waikiki or a casual plate lunch from a food truck near Kapiolani Park — try the classic Hawaiian plate with two scoops of rice, macaroni salad, and your choice of protein
meals.dinner: Orchids at Halekulani or a mid-range option like Arancino at the Kahala — elegant but accessible, with fresh island-inspired cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons at least 2–3 days in advance, especially in peak August season. Children as young as 5 can participate with appropriate instructor ratios. Bring a change of clothes and a towel. Rash guards are recommended to prevent sunburn.

day_by_day.morning: Full-Day Experience: Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center — begin with the cultural village exploration in the morning. The center features seven recreated Pacific Island villages (Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, Tonga, and Marquesas). Families can participate in hands-on cultural demonstrations like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center villages. Watch the world-famous canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular afternoon show featuring traditional songs and dances from across Polynesia. This is a highlight for children and adults alike.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Ali'i Luau Dinner featuring a traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and more. Cap the night with the Ha: Breath of Life show — a breathtaking live theatrical performance with fire dancing, acrobatics, and Polynesian storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departing — the Polynesian Cultural Center is about 35 miles from Waikiki (roughly 1 hour drive)
meals.lunch: Included in the Polynesian Cultural Center all-inclusive package, or dine at their on-site Gateway Restaurant
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner included with the luau package — a lavish spread of traditional Hawaiian and Polynesian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Polynesian Cultural Center package well in advance — it sells out quickly in summer. The all-inclusive Ambassador Package offers the best value for families. Allow at least 7–8 hours for the full experience. The center is located in Laie on Oahu's North Shore.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and resort morning after the big luau day. Sleep in, enjoy breakfast at the resort, and spend the morning at the beachfront. Build sandcastles, collect shells, or simply float in the warm Pacific waters. This is a perfect low-key morning for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa. Drive up to Oahu's North Shore (about 45–60 minutes from Waikiki). Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa, sample Hawaii's legendary shave ice at Matsumoto Shave Ice or Aoki's, browse local boutiques, and discover authentic Hawaiian food culture. Try garlic shrimp from the famous North Shore shrimp trucks.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay on the North Shore — some of the most dramatic and beautiful coastline in all of Hawaii. Watch local surfers (or simply enjoy the scenery) before heading back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a casual café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — a legendary North Shore institution. Try the garlic butter shrimp plate with rice for around $15. Lines move fast and the food is outstanding.
meals.dinner: Kono's Restaurant in Haleiwa for pulled pork burritos and local comfort food, or drive back and dine at a Waikiki favorite like Marukame Udon for affordable, delicious Japanese-Hawaiian udon

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore shrimp trucks are cash-only — bring small bills. Haleiwa is a great place to pick up local souvenirs and Hawaiian-made goods. In August, North Shore waves are typically calm and safe for swimming, unlike winter months. Check surf conditions before letting kids in the water at Waimea or Sunset Beach.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Maui (short 30-minute inter-island flight or book in advance). Begin the legendary Road to Hana Scenic Drive — depart early from the Kahului Airport area. The road winds along Maui's northeastern coastline with 617 curves and 59 bridges. Stop at Twin Falls (easy family-friendly waterfall hike) and the Garden of Eden Arboretum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Wailua Falls, the black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park (book entry reservation in advance), and the charming town of Hana itself. Let the kids splash in natural pools and explore lava rock coastlines.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive or stay overnight in Hana (if budget allows, the Hotel Hana-Maui is a splurge-worthy option). Alternatively, fly back to Oahu and enjoy a relaxed resort evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the airport transfer — or grab pastries and coffee at Kahului Airport Starbucks
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — try fresh banana bread from Aunty Sandy's (a local institution), coconut candy, and tropical fruit from roadside vendors
meals.dinner: Hana Ranch Restaurant in Hana town for local grass-fed beef burgers and Hawaiian plates, or pack a picnic dinner for a scenic roadside stop

day_by_day.notes: Book Waianapanapa State Park entry online in advance — it has a daily visitor reservation system. Start the Road to Hana as early as possible (by 7–8 AM) to avoid traffic and have maximum time at stops. Rent a comfortable SUV or minivan for the family. The drive one-way takes 2.5–3 hours without stops — budget a full day.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Oahu (if you flew to Maui yesterday and came back). Enjoy a relaxed morning at the resort beach. Take a family snorkeling session directly from the beachfront — many Oahu beachfront resorts have accessible reef just offshore. Alternatively, visit Sharks Cove on the North Shore for excellent family snorkeling in calm August conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply meaningful and educational experience for the whole family. The USS Arizona Memorial (accessible by boat), the Battleship Missouri, and the Pacific Aviation Museum are all located here. Allow 3–4 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final relaxed evening in Waikiki. Walk Kalakaua Avenue, enjoy live music at a beachside bar, and let the kids pick out souvenirs from the International Market Place.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up for a full day
meals.lunch: Café at Pearl Harbor visitor center, or pack sandwiches and snacks from a nearby Foodland or Safeway to save money
meals.dinner: Dukes Waikiki or Hula Grill Waikiki — both offer oceanfront dining with fresh Hawaiian fish, burgers, and tropical cocktails in a festive, family-welcoming atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is free to enter, but the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour requires timed-entry tickets — reserve online in advance at recreation.gov. The Battleship Missouri and Aviation Museum have separate admission fees (~$30–$35/adult, less for children). This is a powerful and educational stop appropriate for children ages 8 and up.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning at the resort. Spend quality time at your beachfront location — swim, snorkel, paddleboard (rentals available at most resort beach huts), or simply relax under a palm tree. Let the kids have one last long play session in the Hawaiian surf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. The planetarium, volcano exhibit, and Hawaiian Hall are engaging for all ages. Alternatively, explore Kapiolani Park and the Honolulu Zoo for a relaxed family afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise from Waikiki — book a family-friendly catamaran sunset sail (approximately $40–$60 per adult, less for children). Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the water with Diamond Head in the background — a magical and unforgettable Hawaii memory.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local favorite: Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center — known as one of Oahu's best breakfast spots with creative pancakes and egg dishes
meals.lunch: Helena's Hawaiian Food in Honolulu — a James Beard Award-winning institution serving traditional Hawaiian food including pipikaula (dried beef), lomi salmon, and haupia (coconut pudding)
meals.dinner: Sunset cruise typically includes light pupus (appetizers) and drinks. Follow up with a final dinner at a special restaurant — try Nobu Honolulu for an elevated but accessible splurge, or keep it casual at Yard House in Waikiki

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise in advance — Maitai Catamaran and Na Hoku II are popular, reputable operators departing from Waikiki Beach. Bring a light jacket for the evening breeze on the water. This is a wonderful way to celebrate the end of the trip with the whole family.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up for one final sunrise on the beach — a peaceful, beautiful way to say goodbye to Hawaii. Pack up and check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. If time permits before airport transfer, take a short walk along the shoreline or enjoy a final coffee on the beach lanai.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Honolulu International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and boarding. Browse the airport's local shops for any last-minute souvenirs — Leis, Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and Hawaiian sea salt are all excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with incredible memories, sun-kissed skin, and a heart full of aloha.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or a quick stop at Leonard's Bakery for malasadas (Portuguese-Hawaiian donuts) — a beloved local tradition and the perfect farewell treat
meals.lunch: Airport dining at Honolulu International — try Makai Market food court or grab a bento box from a local vendor inside the terminal
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check your airline's baggage policy if you've accumulated souvenirs — you may need an extra checked bag. Agricultural inspection is mandatory when leaving Hawaii — declare all fresh fruits, plants, and food items. Pineapples purchased from certified vendors are fine to take home. Mahalo and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Hanauma Bay offers calm, clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles, making it perfect for beginner and experienced snorkelers alike. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian culture with a full evening of traditional dance performances, fire knife shows, and an all-you-can-eat Hawaiian feast including kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert. Interactive village exhibits let kids learn about six Pacific Island cultures throughout the day before the evening show.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner surfing lessons with certified instructors on the gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki — considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Group lessons are family-friendly and suitable for children aged 5 and up. Most first-timers stand up on their board within the first session, creating unforgettable memories for the whole family.

experiences.name: Road to Hana Scenic Drive & Waterfalls
experiences.description: Embark on one of the world's most scenic coastal drives along Maui's northeastern coastline, stopping at lush rainforest waterfalls, black sand beaches, and bamboo forests. Family highlights include the Twin Falls swimming hole, Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach, and roadside fruit stands selling fresh coconuts and banana bread. Pack a picnic and make a full day of it.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa
experiences.description: Discover Hawaii's beloved food culture in the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore. Start with the famous rainbow shave ice at Matsumoto's, then explore local food trucks and restaurants serving fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp plates, and acai bowls. The town's laid-back vibe and colorful shops make it a perfect half-day family outing that won't break the budget.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity (tropical fruit platter and champagne) prepared by the resort. Wind down with a late-night stroll along the private beach under the stars.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: In-flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — order the fresh catch of the day with local sides and a bottle of Hawaiian wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in preparation so the suite is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep Day 2 morning light to allow for rest and recovery from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a relaxed orientation walk around the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds, explore the beachfront pool area, and get acquainted with the resort's amenities including the spa and concierge services.
day_by_day.afternoon: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — just a short drive from the resort. Join a private, certified surf instructor session tailored for the whole family on Waikiki's famously gentle waves. Equipment is provided, and the calm conditions make it ideal for first-timers and kids alike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails at the beachfront bar. Enjoy the iconic Hawaiian sunset with handcrafted mai tais and local pupus (appetizers).

meals.breakfast: Oceanfront breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant — fresh açaí bowls, macadamia nut pancakes, Kona coffee, and tropical fruit platters
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at Waikiki — dine at Nobu Honolulu for premium sushi and Japanese-Hawaiian fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients, fresh seafood, and premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book private surf lesson in advance for the family. Apply reef-safe sunscreen throughout the day. Waikiki Beach is approximately 10–15 minutes from most beachfront resorts on Oahu.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — depart early (7:00 AM) to secure entry before the daily visitor cap is reached. Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Crystal-clear waters teem with sea turtles, colorful reef fish, and vibrant coral. Rent premium snorkel gear or bring your own.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed poolside afternoon. Enjoy the resort's private beach — build sandcastles, kayak in calm waters, or book a 60-minute couples or family massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a full evening of authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian cultural performances, traditional fire dancing, hula, and a lavish feast. An unforgettable experience for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at the resort — fresh pastries, fruit, and Kona coffee to fuel the morning adventure
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic-style lunch near Hanauma Bay — pre-arranged premium picnic basket by the resort concierge with gourmet sandwiches, local snacks, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Included in the Luau Dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, fresh fish, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book online at least 2 days ahead as slots fill quickly. The Polynesian Cultural Center is on the North Shore (about 45 minutes from Waikiki); arrange a private luxury van transfer for the family.

day_by_day.morning: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa — head to Oahu's charming North Shore surf town for a guided premium food tour. Sample legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, tropical smoothies, and locally made chocolates and macadamia treats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Haleiwa's boutique shops and art galleries. Visit Waimea Valley for a scenic walk through lush botanical gardens leading to a stunning waterfall — a magical experience for the whole family. Swimming is permitted at the waterfall pool.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private beachfire experience arranged by the resort concierge — roast marshmallows, stargaze, and sip premium Hawaiian craft cocktails on the private beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs Benedict with fresh crab, tropical fruit, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Haleiwa food tour — a curated tasting journey through the town's best local vendors and flavors
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merriman's Honolulu — a renowned farm-to-table restaurant celebrating Hawaii's local farmers and fishermen with an exceptional seasonal menu

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is approximately 45–60 minutes from Waikiki. Arrange a private driver for the day for maximum comfort and flexibility. Waimea Valley has a small entrance fee; the botanical garden walk is easy for all ages.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury catamaran sailing charter departing from Honolulu Harbor. Sail along the stunning Oahu coastline, spot dolphins and humpback whales (seasonal), snorkel in secluded offshore reefs, and enjoy the open ocean breeze. The private charter includes a crew, snorkel gear, and onboard refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore and visit Diamond Head State Monument for a scenic hike to the summit crater rim. The moderately easy trail (1.6 miles round trip) rewards the family with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Ideal for older children and adults.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise along the Waikiki coastline aboard a luxury catamaran — champagne, premium canapés, and a stunning Pacific sunset viewed from the water.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon bagels, avocado toast, acai bowls, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served onboard the private catamaran — fresh sashimi, tropical fruit, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner cruise with premium canapés and champagne, followed by a late dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter and sunset dinner cruise well in advance. Diamond Head hike is best done in the late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. Bring water, hats, and reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (OGG) to Maui — a short 30-minute inter-island flight. Arrange a private luxury SUV transfer to your Maui accommodations (upgrade suite at a partner resort or continue with Aegean Bliss if they have a Maui property). Freshen up and head to Ka'anapali Beach for a morning swim in the crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Road to Hana Scenic Drive — embark on one of the world's most spectacular coastal drives along Maui's northeastern coastline. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, admire the dramatic black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park, and explore lush bamboo forests along the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Hana and enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort. Book a private oceanview cabana for sundowners and a light snack before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick premium breakfast at the resort before departure — avocado toast, fresh fruit, and Kona coffee to go
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort concierge to enjoy along the Road to Hana — artisan sandwiches, local snacks, tropical juices, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's Fish House in Paia, Maui — one of Hawaii's most celebrated restaurants, renowned for ultra-fresh fish caught by local fishermen and a stunning oceanfront setting

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day adventure (approximately 8–10 hours round trip). Book Mama's Fish House well in advance — it is one of the hardest reservations to secure in Hawaii. Waianapanapa State Park requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Haleakalā Crater — depart the resort by 3:30 AM for the drive up to Haleakalā National Park summit (10,023 ft). Watch the breathtaking sunrise above the clouds — a truly once-in-a-lifetime experience. Wrap up in warm layers as summit temperatures can drop to 40°F.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakalā and head to the Maui Ocean Center in Maalaea — one of the finest aquariums in the Pacific. Explore shark tanks, sea turtle exhibits, jellyfish galleries, and an immersive underwater tunnel. Perfect for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort pool and beach. Enjoy a private in-suite dinner experience arranged by the concierge — a personal chef prepares a multi-course Hawaiian feast in your suite with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed gourmet sunrise breakfast box prepared by the resort — thermos of Kona coffee, warm pastries, fresh fruit, and protein bars to enjoy at the summit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Star Noodle in Lahaina — a beloved Maui restaurant serving creative Asian-inspired noodle dishes and small plates with locally sourced ingredients
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience — multi-course Hawaiian tasting menu with fresh seafood, local produce, and premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā sunrise reservations are mandatory and must be booked up to 60 days in advance on recreation.gov. Dress in warm layers — the summit is dramatically colder than the coast. The drive takes approximately 1.5–2 hours from Ka'anapali.

day_by_day.morning: Private snorkeling and dolphin-watching tour off the coast of Maui — depart from Lahaina Harbor on a luxury private boat. Snorkel at Molokini Crater, a partially submerged volcanic caldera teeming with marine life, and Turtle Town for close encounters with Hawaiian green sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic town of Lahaina — stroll Front Street, explore galleries featuring renowned local artists, and visit the iconic 150-year-old Banyan Tree. Shop for premium Hawaiian jewelry, art, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Luau experience at the Old Lahaina Luau — considered the most authentic luau on Maui. Enjoy traditional hula performances, storytelling, and a feast of Hawaiian delicacies in a stunning oceanfront setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — macadamia nut waffles, fresh poke, tropical smoothies, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard the private snorkeling boat — fresh sashimi, tropical fruits, artisan sandwiches, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Included in the Old Lahaina Luau package — traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, lomi salmon, haupia coconut pudding, and tropical cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book Molokini Crater snorkel tour and Old Lahaina Luau well in advance — both are extremely popular and fill up quickly. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for all water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Fly back to Oahu for the final days of the trip. Arrange a private luxury transfer back to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Spend the morning relaxing on the resort's private beachfront — paddleboard, swim, or simply unwind in a luxury cabana with refreshing cocktails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium spa afternoon at the Aegean Bliss Resort spa — book a family spa package with massages, facials, and hydrotherapy treatments. Allow 2–3 hours for a full rejuvenating experience before the final evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktail hour at the resort's rooftop or beachfront bar. Reflect on the journey with handcrafted Hawaiian cocktails and premium pupus as the sun dips below the Pacific horizon.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the Maui resort before departure
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh poke bowls, lobster rolls, tropical salads, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Alan Wong's Honolulu — one of Hawaii's most iconic fine dining establishments, celebrating Hawaii Regional Cuisine with inventive dishes and exceptional service

day_by_day.notes: Confirm inter-island flight timing to maximize beach and spa time upon return. Alan Wong's reservations should be booked well in advance. Consider purchasing premium local gifts and souvenirs (Kona coffee, Hawaiian honey, macadamia chocolates) for loved ones at home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy one last sunrise walk along the private beach. Take a final swim in the ocean or pool. Pack and prepare for checkout. Visit the resort gift shop for any last-minute Hawaiian keepsakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (arrange with concierge in advance). Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport. Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium lounge access before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with unforgettable memories. Settle into your premium cabin for a comfortable journey home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a grand spread of Hawaiian favorites: fresh poke, tropical fruits, Kona coffee, macadamia nut pancakes, and fresh-squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or at the airport's premium lounge before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining in premium or business class

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout (12:00–2:00 PM) from the resort to maximize the final morning. Confirm all luggage, souvenirs, and travel documents before departure. Arrange private airport transfer at least one day in advance.
